short: Scottish philosopher whose book The Wealth of Nations laid the foundations of modern economics.
full:
Adam Smith was a leading figure of the Scottish Enlightenment who initially gained prominence as a moral philosopher with his 1759 work, The Theory of Moral Sentiments. He spent years travelling across Europe and observing the early stages of industrialisation before publishing his magnum opus, An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations, in 1776.

The book provided the first comprehensive, systematic explanation of capitalist economics, arguing that free markets, guided by an 'invisible hand' of self-interest, naturally allocate resources more efficiently than state-directed mercantilism. His theories on the division of labour, free trade, and the limits of government intervention profoundly shaped nineteenth-century economic policy and remain foundational to modern classical economics.
